name: Nurlan Morita-Antwi
role: Prototype theft and corporate tech acquisition — tech retriever
location: Old Harbor — repurposed shipping infrastructure turned black market hub
description:
Nurlan Morita-Antwi is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 31, the augmentation scarring around her temples and jawline tells a story of installation by someone who prioritized function over aesthetics. The chrome is visible — vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see her surpass them. She works as a tech retriever out of Old Harbor, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Nurlan Morita-Antwi lacks in subtlety, she compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.

core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
That the work they do makes the city worse, not better
Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
coping_mechanisms: Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it
Compartmentalization — work feelings and personal feelings exist in separate boxes
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
blind_spots: Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
psychology.secret: Nurlan Morita-Antwi is in augmentation debt to a corporate subsidiary — Φ180,000 outstanding — and the interest is compounding. If they miss a payment, a kill team comes.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Uses old pre-collapse slang that nobody else remembers
Pauses mid-sentence to listen — combat habit that bleeds into conversation
example_lines: "Corporate R&D security is built to stop amateurs. I'm a professional."
"The prototype is worth more than both our lives combined. Handle it carefully."
"I steal things that haven't been invented yet. The future is always in transit."

story_hooks: A Tier 4 executive offers Nurlan Morita-Antwi a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
Nurlan Morita-Antwi's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
A dead drop Nurlan Morita-Antwi maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
narrative_function: Nurlan Morita-Antwi represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Her stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Vocal modulator — can replicate any voice after 30 seconds of sample audio. Thermal masking system — body heat signature can be suppressed or spoofed
daily_life: Keeps a rigid daily structure — wake, train, check contracts, maintain gear, sleep. The structure is a defense against the chaos of the work. Deviations from the schedule are a warning sign that something is wrong.

weaknesses: risk-averse to the point of missed opportunities

decision_rules: Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
habits: Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
breaking_points: Complete isolation — cut off from network, contacts, and purpose simultaneously
Being forced to choose between a crew member and the mission — and choosing wrong
